candidates.label: Public health, disease prevention and biomedical intervention

concepts.label: Human biology, disease and biomedical research
concepts.concept: Combines molecular and cellular biology, anatomy, physiology, infection, immunity, pharmacology and disease mechanisms with laboratory work, statistics, evidence synthesis and ethics. Neuroscience adds a neural view of human illness. It approaches the biomedical core while leaving substantial differences in specialised laboratory training and compulsory independent research.

concepts.label: Public health, disease prevention and biomedical intervention
concepts.concept: Connects biological disease mechanisms with population patterns, prevention and intervention. Epidemiology, health psychology, sociology and qualitative research develop health-context inquiry; public economics examines health spending and policy. Laboratory, statistical and evidence-synthesis work retains a biomedical research core. Persuasion methods add communication practice through sustainability projects, rather than a promised clinical campaign.

concepts.label: Biomedical inquiry, data and modelling
concepts.concept: Connects molecular, physiological, immune and disease study with experimental statistics, programming, machine learning, neural networks, linear algebra, numerical methods and signal systems. These general computational tools support quantitative biomedical questions; the selected courses do not promise clinical datasets, a dedicated diagnostic imaging programme or completion of Leiden’s research project.

selection.assessment: Three sequentially supportedprogrammes retain a directbiomedical core and actuallaboratory/methods work. Populationhealth adds coherent social/prevention/intervention tools; quantitative study adds actualmath/data/computation. Pairwise52.5/30/75ECdifferences follow theseconcepts. No specialistoncology,advancedpathology orcompulsorysupervisedresearch equivalence; no fourthcareer/example-drivenroute.
